title: Direct Trust of Client-Manipulable Cookies
pattern: Relying directly on values extracted from client-side cookies, query parameters, or hidden fields to enforce business invariants (like prices, roles, or quantities).
why_bad: HTTP clients can easily manipulate cookie payloads using browsers or intercepting proxies. Adversaries can modify data (e.g. altering the price of an item to `$0.01`) to subvert pricing, roles, or inventory rules.
detection: Deserializing client-supplied string inputs (cookies, headers, query strings) directly into model structures that govern pricing or access privileges without database cross-verification.
fix: Store only a random, unpredictable session token on the client side; maintain all transactional data, roles, and pricing variables strictly on the server database.
